newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Rugby union-Dominguez aids Italy recognition bid.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Dominguez aids Italy recognition bid.

text.p: Fly-half Diego Dominguez scored 22 points as Italy stunned Ireland with a 37-29 win in freezing weather at Lansdowne Road on Saturday to enhance their claims for a place in an expanded Five Nations rugby union championship.
"I think we are ready to compete in a tournament like the Five Nations," said captain and prop forward Massimo Cuttitta, scorer of one of Italy's four tries.
Coach Georges Coste commented: "We will do everything we can to merit inclusion in a tournament like the Five Nations. We have enormous potential, although we still need to work to fulfill it."

Ireland manager Pat Whelan was downcast at the result which followed home defeats by Western Samoa and Australia in the run up to the Five Nations championship starting later this month and for which bookmakers have made them 14-1 outsiders.
"It is demoralising for young lads, and ours is a young team, to continually lose games. But we have no excuses. We were beaten by the better team on the day," he said.
It was appropriate that it was Dominguez who finally made the game safe for the Italians when he went over in the right corner for a try in the 79th minute.
Dominguez, who was the best player on view, added the conversion to leave Ireland in disarray ahead of their opening Five Nations championship game at home to France in two weeks time.
The Italian fly-half had also been at the centre of things in the 62nd minute when he put right winger Paolo Vaccari in for his second try of the match to give the visitors a 30-29 point lead.

Ireland looked to have taken control early in the third-quarter when fly-half Paul Burke and Dominguez swopped penalties before centre Jonathan Bell scored his side's only try to put the home side 26-20 ahead.
The Irish maintained this advantage, with the two fly-halves again swopping penalties, before the game swung in the Italians favour with Vaccari pouncing for his second try.

Burke had kept Ireland in the game in the first half when he kicked six penalties from seven attempts at goal while Italy caused their hosts all sorts of problems with their aggressive running and accurate passing.

Italy scored two tries in the first half through the impressive Vaccari and Massimo Cuttitta. Dominguez converted both and landed a penalty to leave Italy just a point behind at 18-17 at the interval.

Ireland - 15-Conor O'Shea; 14-James Topping, 13-Jonathan Bell, 12-Mark McCall, 11-Dominic Crotty; 10-Paul Burke, 9-Stephen McIvor; 8-Anthony Foley, 7-Eric Miller (18-Denis McBride, 33), 6-David Corkery, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Gabriel Fulcher (19-Paddy Johns, 66), 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Keith Wood (captain), 1-Nick Popplewell.

Italy - 15-Javier Pertile; 14-Paolo Vaccari, 13-Stefano Bordon, 12-Allesandro Stoica, 11-Marcello Cuttita (21-Nicola Mazzucato, 44); 10-Diego Dominquez, 9-Alessandro Troncon; 8-Orazio Arancio, 7-Julian Gardner, 6-Andrea Sgorlon, 5-Walter Cristofoletto (18-Carlo Checcinato, 66), 4-Gianbattista Croci, 3-Franco Properzi-Curti, 2-Carlo Orlandi, 1-Massimo Cuttitta (captain).
